## Files matching `runtime-catalog/src/**`

### Build & Test Commands

```bash
# Build (checkstyle runs automatically at compile phase)
mvn package

# Build without tests
mvn package -DskipTests

# Run all tests
mvn test

# Run a single test class
mvn test -Dtest=ChainElementDifferenceServiceTest

# Run a single test method
mvn test -Dtest=ChainElementDifferenceServiceTest#testMethodName

# Test coverage report (target/site/jacoco/index.html)
mvn verify

# Run locally with dev profile (debug port 18085)
mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=development

# Checkstyle only
mvn checkstyle:check

# Regenerate the service export/import golden corpus (schemas/src/test/resources/exportimport-golden/)
# GoldenCorpusCapture sits outside Surefire's include patterns, so the suite never runs it.
mvn test -Dtest=GoldenCorpusCapture#capturePost553 -DfailIfNoTests=false
mvn test -Dtest=GoldenCorpusCapture#capturePost553Dotted -DfailIfNoTests=false
```

`pom.xml` puts `../schemas/src/main/resources/qip-model/*service.schema.yaml` on the **test** classpath through a
`<testResource>`. There is still no Maven dependency on `qip-schemas`, but editing a service schema in the `schemas`
module can now fail `mvn test` here — `ServiceTypeFilesTest` compares each schema against `IntegrationSystemType`.

Three more shared corpora live in `schemas` and are read here the same way. Two of them — the conformance corpus and
the export/import golden archives — are output **this** module produces, stored there because a second module reads
them; a capture therefore writes across the module boundary. `schemas/**` is in this module's CI `paths:` filter for
all of it.

- **The golden archives** (`schemas/src/test/resources/exportimport-golden`, on the classpath as
  `/exportimport-golden`). Four archive trees this module's serializer chain produced; the VS Code extension opens two
  of them. See the README beside them for which sets are regenerable and which are historical captures.
- **The naming corpus** (`schemas/src/test/resources/naming`, on the classpath as `/naming`). `ServiceNameCorpusTest`
  measures this module's three name generators, both id extractors and discovery against a rule the corpus declares,
  and the VS Code extension measures itself against the same file. It is the only cross-language check of the file
  names — renaming one postfix constant reddens 21 cases here and none in the extension without it. A `classify`
  outcome that disagrees between the two sides needs a written `divergence` in the corpus, not a fix on either side.
- **Three frozen-copy tests in the `naming` package measure what an *older* build does with an archive this one
  writes**; never update a frozen copy to match current code — that deletes the measurement. Every other compatibility
  assertion here is written in terms of today's code. `PreS553DiscoveryCompatibilityTest` freezes
  `extractSystemsFromImportDirectory` at `8285c644b~1` and asserts the exact found/missed partition per
  `(golden tree, postfix)`. `PreS553MigrationBarrierCompatibilityTest` freezes main's migration barrier
  (`FrozenMigrationBarrier`, registries V100–V102) and type assignment: a current archive fails per service on the
  unknown versions `{103,104,105}` and is never mistyped, while `legacy-flat` passes the barrier and types from
  `integrationSystemType` — the downgrade bridge, proven at the file level. `S553TypeResolverCompatibilityTest`
  freezes the #553-era resolver from `2934600a6` (name first, then the body field, never `$schema`): a current plain
  archive fails per service with the actionable message, never silently.

`ServiceFormatConvergenceTest` is the fixed point: export, import, export again, compare the unpacked trees. The
current format is stable from the first export; the legacy format is not, and deliberately so — it writes each
operation's raw `specification`, which the current format omits, so the import fills it and the second export writes
it. That converges after one round trip, and both halves are asserted separately rather than papered over.

After renaming or regenerating a golden fixture, run `mvn clean`: `target/test-classes` keeps the old copy, and a test
then runs against a tree the sources do not hold.

The golden corpus has four sets. `post553` and `post553-dotted` are regenerable with the commands above;
`pre553-current` and `legacy-flat` are historical captures that only a pre-#553 checkout can produce, and
`GoldenCorpusCapture` refuses to overwrite them from this one. `post553-dotted` is its own set rather than a fourth
service in `post553` because `legacyExportIsUnchanged` and `currentExportMatchesTheRecordedFormat` compare a fresh
export file for file against a captured set in **both** formats — anything added to the shared fixture reddens the two
sets nothing can regenerate.

**`golden/post553` and `golden/post553-dotted` have a consumer in another module.** `vscode-extension`'s
`pretest:integration` copies both trees into its integration workspace (`scripts/copy-backend-fixtures.mjs`), so moving
or renaming them breaks that run, and regenerating them is what carries a format change across to the extension —
`ServiceExportFormatTest`'s two pins are what force the regeneration in the first place. The extension's CI `paths:`
filter needs no entry of its own for them — `schemas/**` covers the trees where they now live. `infrastructure/test-service-type-roundtrip.sh` covers the same format against a running stack, including the
`QIP_EXPORT_LEGACY_FORMAT=true` downgrade.

### Architecture Overview

**Single-module Spring Boot 3.5 application** (Java 21, Maven) that serves as the runtime catalog for the Qubership Integration Platform. It manages integration chains, deployments, and library elements, publishing deployment configurations to Consul for consumption by the Integration Engine.

#### Key Layers

- **REST controllers** (`rest/v1`, `rest/v2`, `rest/v3`) — versioned API; v3 is the latest with session-based import/export
- **Services** (`service/`) — core business logic: chain compilation, deployment building, import/export with versioned migrations, spec parsing (OpenAPI/GraphQL/WSDL/Protobuf)
- **Persistence** (`persistence/`) — JPA entities and Spring Data repositories; PostgreSQL with `catalog` schema
- **Builder** (`builder/`) — generates Apache Camel XML routes from chain definitions using Handlebars templates
- **Mapper** (`mapper/`) — AtlasMap-based field mapping (JSON, XML, GraphQL, gRPC)
- **Consul** (`consul/`) — publishes compiled deployments and listens for library events

#### Important Subsystems

- **Deployment pipeline**: Chain → compiler → Camel XML builder (Handlebars) → Consul publish
- **Import/Export**: Session-based (v3) with versioned migration chain (`service/exportimport/migrations/`)
- **Element definitions**: ~70+ integration element types defined as resources in `src/main/resources/elements/`, each with descriptor JSON and Handlebars templates
- **DB migrations**: Flyway at `src/main/resources/db/migration/postgresql/configs/` (V100+). Spring Boot's Flyway is off (`spring.flyway.enabled: false`, `FlywayAutoConfiguration` excluded); `FlywayInitializer.migrate()` (`@PostConstruct`, gated on `qip.standalone`) runs it and registers Java migrations only from the injected `List<ConfigsJavaMigration>` beans. A concrete `ConfigsJavaMigration` (e.g. `V112_001__BackfillTypedOperations`, the first one) MUST be a `@Component`, or it never runs — the classpath location scan looks in package `db.migration.postgresql.configs`, not the `org.qubership...` package where the class lives, so `setJavaMigrations` is the sole registration. The `V<major>_<minor>__` class name needs `@SuppressWarnings("checkstyle:TypeName")`.
- **On-demand operation schemas**: as of `V112_000`, the `operations` table no longer stores `request_schema` / `response_schemas`. `OperationSchemaExtractor` rebuilds them on read from the raw `specification_source`, reusing each protocol's persistence-free `parseOperations(..., withSchemas)` core (the same core import calls with `withSchemas = false`). On `Operation` the two fields are `@Transient`; `OperationService.getOperationWithSchemas` populates them before the MapStruct mappers run. `getOperationWithSchemas` is `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`, so the parse runs inside one short read-only transaction; specs are small enough that holding the connection is acceptable. Schemas are re-parsed per read (no cache); the shared conformance corpus in `schemas/src/test/resources/conformance` is the parity oracle (`OperationSchemaExtractorParityTest`). Extraction runs only on the `OperationController` read surface plus DDS — `SnapshotService` never calls the extractor, so compile/snapshot/Consul publish are unaffected.
- **Typed operations**: per-protocol operation data lives in `Operation.typed` (`jsonb`), the source of truth; `method` and `path` stay as derived columns, recomputed in `setTyped` and backed by a `@PrePersist`/`@PreUpdate` net for entities mutated elsewhere. Derivation runs in the setter, not only on persist, because `OperationSchemaExtractor` matches unpersisted operations on `getMethod`/`getPath`. `TypedOperation` is a sealed interface over five records (openapi, asyncapi, wsdl, graphql, protobuf); each carries `@JsonTypeName` because hypersistence serializes jsonb by the runtime type, not the declared one. All five parsers emit `typed` at import; `V112_001__BackfillTypedOperations` fills pre-existing rows column-derived. The conformance corpus (`schemas/src/test/resources/conformance`) is the parity oracle — derived `method`/`path` must match byte for byte (`TypedOperationBackfillParityTest`).
- **Protocol schema matrix**: HTTP (OpenAPI 3.0/3.1/3.2, Swagger 2.0) and AsyncAPI (Kafka + AMQP, 2.6/3.0) extract non-empty schemas; gRPC (`.proto`, the pure-Java Wire parser, no `protoc` needed) extracts non-empty from a `specification_source` row. SOAP and METAMODEL are null-by-design (`OperationSchemaExtractor.hasNoSchemaExtraction`); GraphQL goes through the parser but yields nothing useful. A corrupt or unmatched source degrades gracefully to `200` + null schemas + `log.warn` (never a 500) for every protocol.
- **MaaS classifier resolution is deploy-time, not snapshot-time.** `MaasClassifierHelper`
  (`cr/sources/builders/xml/beans/builders/element/helpers/`) resolves the classifier while the Camel XML is built:
  for a service-call or async-api element it reads `ElementUtils.extractOperationAsyncProperties(element)`; for a
  Kafka or AMQP element it reads the element's own `maas.*.classifier.name` property, gated on
  `connectionSourceType` being `MAAS` or `MAAS_BY_CLASSIFIER`. Read classifier data through
  `ElementUtils.extractOperationAsyncProperties` — never `getPropertyAsString` plus a cast on a nested `Map`, which
  throws `ClassCastException` once the property is actually present. `SnapshotService` holds no MaaS code and
  `EnvironmentMapper` has no `@AfterMapping` write-back: the typed-DTO and snapshot-denormalization design described
  in `docs/plans/completed/20260710-maas-classifier-typed-home.md` is not what shipped.
- **The classifier name has one home, the scope has another.** The name lives on the element (put there from the
  operation's `x-maas-classifier-name`) and is read from there by every consumer: `MaasClassifierHelper`, the
  `Kafka`/`RabbitMqElementPropertiesBuilder`, `OperationElementPropertiesVerifier`, the design generators, the chain
  filter. Nothing writes `maas.classifier.name` onto an environment, so do not reintroduce an environment fallback
  for it — the classic (Consul) deploy path never honored one, and the lookup it needs both crashes on an environment
  whose `properties` jsonb is null (auto-created environments have one) and throws `EntityNotFoundException` when the
  active environment is gone. The *scope* around the name is the opposite: `maas.classifier.namespace` /
  `.tenantId` / `.tenantEnabled` are read from the active environment for async elements (dotted keys, authored by the
  environment form) and from the element itself for standalone Kafka/AMQP elements (`maasClassifier*` camelCase keys).

#### Code Generation & Processing

- **ANTLR4** generates visitors (grammar sources processed at build time)
- **MapStruct** for DTO/entity mapping (configured with Lombok binding)
- **Hibernate bytecode enhancement** enabled for lazy initialization

### Conventions

- **Conventional Commits** required for all commits and PRs
- **Checkstyle** enforced at compile time (rules from `qubership-integration-checkstyle` artifact)
- **Naming**: Hibernate uses `CamelCaseToSnakeCase` physical naming strategy
- **API group**: `ApiGroup` (table `api_group`, labels `api_group_labels`) is the Service → API group → API →
  Operation hierarchy level between `IntegrationSystem` and `SystemModel` (the "Api" DTO/UI name). It was renamed from
  `SpecificationGroup`; the v1 REST paths, request parameters, and DTO JSON properties still use the old
  `specificationGroup*` spelling for backward compatibility. Rename fallout that is easy to miss:
  - **File names**: export writes `{id}.api-group.{app}.yaml` (`API_GROUP_FILE_POSTFIX`); `qip.export.legacy-format=true`
    keeps the flat `specGroup-` prefix deliberately. `ServiceDeserializer` discovery reads all three (the legacy
    prefix plus the `.specification-group.` and `.api-group.` postfixes), and dropping one imports a service with no
    groups, silently. There is no `apiGroup-` prefix anywhere.
  - **Import migrations**: `V104ServiceImportFileMigration` renames `content.specificationGroups` →
    `content.apiGroups` before `ServiceDeserializer` reads it; `V104RevertMigration` undoes it for the legacy export
    format. A revert migration must also strip its own version from `content.migrations`, or a re-import computes an
    empty version set and the forward migration never fires. Which documents a revert migration owns is
    `ServiceDocumentMatcher`'s call, shared by V103, V104, and V105: it matches `$schema` against the service, the
    three per-type service, context-service, and MCP-service URIs. Matching on content fields instead misses a bare
    service — the export DTO is `@JsonInclude(NON_EMPTY)` and never fills `apiGroups` — and an unstripped version makes
    a pre-rename QIP reject the whole archive as "exported from a newer version".
  - **Rollout import**: a package carries no version data, so `ServiceConfigurationsToFilesConverter` stamps
    `content.migrations` itself. It stamps only the versions whose migration is unsafe to re-run
    (`MigrationUtil.formatAppliedVersions`); claiming a version it never applied would skip that migration for the
    whole rollout path, which is how V104 stopped firing there. A migration safe to re-run says so through
    `ImportFileMigration.isIdempotent()`. `IntegrationSystemContentDto.apiGroups` also carries
    `@JsonAlias("specificationGroups")`, and `ServiceDeserializer` reads the inline list under both names.
  - **Instruction file**: the section is `apiGroups`, with `@JsonAlias("specificationGroups")` on
    `GeneralImportInstructionsConfig` so older files still load.
  - **Enum value** `SPECIFICATION_GROUP` → `API_GROUP` on `EntityType`, `ImportEntityType`, and `FilterFeature`. Only
    `FilterFeature` has a `@JsonAlias`; two filter paths compare raw strings and never reach Jackson, so they translate
    by hand: `ActionLogFilterRepositoryImpl.parseEntityType` and
    `ImportInstructionFilterSpecificationBuilder.normalizeEntityTypeFilterValue` (the latter per comma-separated
    element, for `IN`/`NOT_IN`)
  - **Schema config**: `qip.json.schemas.api-group` / `API_GROUP_JSON_SCHEMA_URI` in `src/main/resources/application.yml`,
    alongside the retained `qip.json.schemas.specification-group`
- **Service type**: a plain service file states its type in its **`$schema`** — not in its file name, and not in
  `content.integrationSystemType`, which the exporter no longer writes (`@JsonProperty(access = WRITE_ONLY)` on
  `IntegrationSystemContentDto` — not `@JsonIgnore`, which would also stop deserializing every pre-#553 archive).
  #553 put the type in the name; that was reverted because a name is a poor place to carry it, and the three per-type
  schemas — the part of #553 worth keeping — identify the type on their own. `ServiceTypeFiles` is the one place that
  knows how a type is spelled in a `$schema` and in a document (`typeFromDocument`, shared by the import preview and
  the rollout converter); import, export, and the V105 revert migration read it from there, so the spellings cannot
  drift apart. V105 forward never touches it — it is a pure no-op.
  - **File names state a kind, never a type.** Export writes `{id}.service.{app}.yaml` for all three plain types
    (`ExportImportUtils.generateMainSystemFileExportName`, which takes no type at all);
    `qip.export.legacy-format=true` keeps the flat `service-{id}.yaml`. The three per-type postfixes still exist and
    are still discovered, because archives exported during #553 carry them
    (`SystemExportImportService.SERVICE_FILE_POSTFIXES` through the multi-postfix
    `ExportImportUtils.extractSystemsFromImportDirectory`) — a **read-only** format, and not a type source. The
    single-postfix overload stays for the context and MCP import services; do not reach for it here, because it ORs
    the legacy prefix into every scan that asks for a plain-service postfix, so one call per postfix returns every
    legacy-named file four times and imports it four times.
  - **Two matching layers on `$schema`** (`ServiceTypeFiles.typeFromSchemaUri`): the configured
    `qip.json.schemas.*` value first, then the schema's own file name with every extension off. The URI is
    configurable on both sides — the VS Code extension stamps whatever a project's `.config.qip.yaml` holds — so the
    second layer is what carries a document between two installations configured differently, and what reads the
    older truncated form that stops at `.../external-service`. A project that renames the schema *file* resolves no
    type, and the import says so rather than guessing. The extension resolves it identically
    (`serviceFileType.ts:serviceTypeFromSchema`), and `schemas/src/test/resources/naming` declares the rule for both.
    `isContextOrMCPServiceFile` deliberately keeps an exact-URI comparison instead: a file it answers true for is
    handed to another import entirely, so a loose match there loses a service rather than mistyping one.
  - **The postfix is read only where it is written** — in the segment right after the id, by
    `ExportImportUtils.statesPostfix`, which discovery calls. Scanning the whole name instead lets the app prefix
    (`app.prefix`, appended behind the postfix) claim a postfix of its own, which pulled files into the wrong scan.
    The id therefore has to be one dot-free segment, the
    same shape `extractSystemIdFromFileName` assumes. The three current-format service name generators — the plain one
    shared by all three types, plus the context and MCP ones — refuse an id that is not
    (`ExportImportUtils.requireCurrentFormatId`, gated on `fitsCurrentFormatFileName`) rather than writing a name whose
    leading segment reads back as another id. The api, api-group, and specification name generators carry no such
    check. Only the plain service has a legacy flat name import discovers, so only
    its refusal points at `QIP_EXPORT_LEGACY_FORMAT=true`; nothing scans for `context-service-<id>.yaml` or
    `mcp-service-<id>.yaml`, in this version or any older one, which is also why that flag is **not** a downgrade path
    for a context or MCP service. `ServiceConfigurationsToFilesConverter` holds the same rule: the plain path falls
    back to the flat name, the context path skips the service with a `log.error`.
  - **Discovery reads the postfix after the directory name too** (`statesPostfix(File, String)`, the overload only the
    archive walk calls). A pre-#553 QIP wrote `services/a.b/a.b.service.qip.yaml` for a dotted id, and anchoring on
    the first dot alone walked past it — no row, no log, for a file every earlier version imported. Every export and
    the rollout converter name that directory after the service, so the directory reads such an id back. It does not
    reopen the name to the rest of the archive: an api group whose app prefix spells a service postfix is named after
    the group, not after the service.
  - **A refusal costs one service, never the archive.** The file name is built inside the loop over every service, so
    a throw that escaped it returned an error and no archive at all from `GET|POST /v1/export/system` — the one
    endpoint for getting data out of an installation. `ServiceSerializer` calls
    `ExportImportUtils.requireExportableServiceId` before the loop and `SystemExportImportService.exportOneSystem`
    drops that row with a `log.error`; `ArchiveWriter` catches `ServiceExportException` per exported object, which is
    what covers the context and MCP exports, whose names have no such pre-flight. The same rule covers the null-type refusal. The export action
    log records only the rows the archive holds, and an export with nothing left answers 204.
  - **The postfix, not the `service-` prefix, tells the two name formats apart** (`isLegacyFlatServiceName`): a name
    stating a **plain-service** postfix right after the id is current-format whatever the id starts with, and only a
    name stating none of the four is the flat `service-<id>.yaml`. An id wearing that prefix is ordinary —
    `DiscoveryService` takes the id from the Kubernetes service name, so a cloud service named `service-orders` has one
    — and refusing it on export made that service unexportable and aborted the whole archive, since the refusal is not
    per service. The two shapes are genuinely ambiguous (`service-orders.internal-service.qip.yaml` parses both ways),
    so the loser is the flat name of an id whose *second* segment spells a plain-service postfix:
    `requireLegacyFlatId` refuses to write it.
  - **Only the four plain-service postfixes are weighed there**, from `ExportImportUtils.plainServicePostfixes()`,
    which is also what `SystemExportImportService.SERVICE_FILE_POSTFIXES` is. The flat name is the plain service's own
    second format, and nothing discovers `context-service-<id>.yaml` or `mcp-service-<id>.yaml`, so
    `extractSystemsFromImportDirectory` ORs the flat branch into a plain-service scan only — a scan is that one when
    its requested postfixes include a plain-service one. Weighing `.context-service.` and `.mcp-service.` in
    `isLegacyFlatServiceName` too made `service-orders.context-service.qip.yaml` current-format, and the plain-service
    scan, which carries neither postfix, walked past a name every earlier version discovered. That name is claimed by
    two imports on purpose: the context import reads it as the context file of `service-ctx`
    (`extractSystemIdFromCurrentFormatFileName`, which the context and MCP paths use because their names have no flat
    form), and the plain-service import reads it as the flat name of `ctx.context-service.qip`. No formulation reads
    both ids out of one string, and dropping either claim loses a file some archive already holds.
  - **The document decides which of the two claims ends in a row.** `SystemExportImportService` filters every
    discovered file through `ServiceTypeFiles.isContextOrMCPServiceFile` before the collision split: a name stating a
    context or MCP postfix over a document whose `$schema` is that kind's — the same check `isContextServiceFile` and
    `isMCPServiceFile` run — is left to that import with no row at all. Reporting it as `ImportSystemStatus.ERROR`
    instead made `ImportResult.hasErrors()` true after the context service had been created correctly, so
    `RolloutImportService` sent a FAILED callback and `GET /v3/import/{id}` answered 207 for an import that succeeded.
    The row survives where no other import has the file — an unrecognized `$schema`, or none — and
    `ServiceDeserializer.otherKindHint` still names the import it may belong to. On the archive import path this is the
    only use of `$schema`, and it asks which *kind* of document this is, never which of the three plain types. Only a name that
    could be a context or MCP one has its document read (`ServiceTypeFiles.statesContextOrMCPPostfix`, the cheap half of
    the check): every other file is answered from the name and reaches the import unparsed, so an archive is not parsed
    twice.
  - **Type resolution** is `ServiceDeserializer.resolveServiceType`, which runs for every document, migrated or not,
    over the raw node read off disk: `$schema` first, `content.integrationSystemType` second (a pre-#553 document
    carries the plain service schema and states its type there), then a `ServiceImportException`. A `$schema` and a
    field that disagree raise as well, rather than letting one win. The **file name is not read at all** — it stated a
    type only between #553 and this version, and such a file carries the matching `$schema` anyway, so a per-type name
    over a document stating nothing is an error row, not a guess. The same
    `ServiceTypeFiles.typeFromSchemaUri` also serves the two places that hold a document and no
    QIP-written file name: `V105RevertMigration`, and the rollout import, where `ImportConfigFactory.isService` routes
    the three per-type URIs into the service bucket (leave them out and such an item falls through every branch and is
    dropped in silence) and `ServiceConfigurationsToFilesConverter` falls back to `$schema` for the type when
    `content.integrationSystemType` is absent, which a conformant post-#553 package always is. Which *kind* of document
    a file holds is a different question, and `$schema` is how the context and MCP imports have always answered it (see
    the two claims above).
  - **V105 forward is a no-op on purpose.** `V105ServiceImportFileMigration.makeMigration` returns the node untouched —
    resolution already happened above, and the version stamp is the class's whole reason to exist. Delete it as an empty
    migration and the compatibility barrier goes with it. An old QIP now **discovers** today's plain services again —
    the name went back to `.service.`, which its scan has always matched, so `PreS553DiscoveryCompatibilityTest`
    records a found set where #553 recorded an empty one. What it makes of them is the barrier's job: it reads no type
    off a document whose `content.integrationSystemType` is absent and reports 105 as a version it does not know, so
    the row is an `ImportSystemStatus.ERROR` rather than a file it walks past in silence.
  - **V105 revert is broad-match, narrow-write.** `supportsDocument` delegates to `ServiceDocumentMatcher`, so the 105
    strip also reaches the context and MCP services stamped from the same list; the type field and the plain `$schema`
    are written only for the three per-type URIs, or a context service acquires a service type it never had. Gating the
    whole migration narrowly instead is circular — `revert()` never runs on a document `supportsDocument` rejected.
    Restoring the plain `$schema` is what keeps V104 and V103 matching afterwards (`FileMigrationService` sorts reverts
    by version descending and re-evaluates `supportsDocument` on each intermediate result), and it is why
    `ServiceDocumentMatcher`'s URI set had to learn the three per-type URIs.
  - **The type is immutable.** `SystemController.updateSystem` answers 404 on an unknown id instead of falling through
    to create; `mergeWithoutLabels` and `patchMergeWithoutLabels` map no type; `validateServiceTypeUnchanged` refuses an
    import that would switch one. A stored null is a legacy row that never had a type, so an import that states one
    repairs it.
  - **The `integration_system_type` column stays** — #553 changed the file format, not the runtime. Per-type rules that
    are pure data live on `IntegrationSystemType` (`allowedProtocols()`, `maxEnvironments()`, both exhaustive switches
    with no `default`), and `EnvironmentLimitUtils.validate` (`util/`, not a bean) drives all three call sites from
    them: import update, import create, and `EnvironmentController`. `EnvironmentLimitUtils.violation` is the
    non-throwing form `ServiceSerializer` warns from, so an over-populated row still exports. A null type is tolerated
    on those paths but refused on export — `IntegrationSystemDtoMapper.requireType` raises `ServiceExportException`
    instead of NPE-ing later in `EntityType.getSystemType` — and that refusal drops the one row, not the archive.
  - Deliberate asymmetry with the VS Code extension: a type-less file stays visible there under `Unknown` and
    editable, while this service refuses the same file on import — tolerant editor, strict backend. **Shipped.** The
    extension reads and writes all three typed names, groups them in its tree, and converts a legacy `.service.` file
    on its first write.
- Tests use `@ExtendWith(SpringExtension.class)` with `@ContextConfiguration` (lightweight, no full app context); test resources include both `src/test/resources` and `src/main/resources`

### Local stack quirks

Two behaviors of the local Docker stack look like defects in this service but are not:

- The `qip-runtime-catalog` image ships no `/usr/bin/protoc`, so a fresh gRPC (`.proto`) import or an export/import
  round trip fails. Read-path schema extraction still works from a `specification_source` row, because the pure-Java
  Wire parser needs no `protoc`.
- `POST /v1/catalog/domains/{domain}/deployments/update` in full-request mode (`excludeDeployments: []`) is served
  from a per-domain in-memory cache that only a Consul-watched key invalidates. This dev stack's Consul KV never
  changes, so the cache goes stale after the first call. Pass a bogus `excludeDeployments` entry to force the
  uncached delta path.

### Platform Context

This service is the **central brain** of the Qubership Integration Platform (QIP). See `README.md` for the repository layout.

#### Direct Dependencies (this service consumes)

| Service | Protocol | What For |
|---|---|---|
| **Consul** | REST (`/v1/kv/*`, `/v1/txn`) | Publish compiled deployment configs, listen for library events, configuration at `config/{NAMESPACE}/` |
| **PostgreSQL** | JDBC | Primary data store (schema: `catalog`). Chains, elements, deployments, snapshots, specs, action logs, import sessions. |
| **Engine pods** | REST (direct pod IPs via Kubernetes API) | `GET /v1/engine/live-exchanges` — fetch running exchanges; `DELETE /v1/engine/live-exchanges/{id}/{id}` — kill exchanges |
| **Kubernetes API** | kubernetes-client-java | Discover engine pods/deployments by label `qip_engine_app`, get domain info |

#### Services That Depend on This

| Service | How |
|---|---|
| **Engine / Micro Engine** | Fetches deployment descriptors via `POST /v1/catalog/domains/{domain}/deployments/update` and library JARs via `GET /v1/models/{id}/dto/jar` |
| **Sessions Management** | Resolves chainId → chainName via `GET /v1/chains/names` |
| **UI** | Calls catalog, variables-management, and systems-catalog APIs via Nginx proxy |

#### Key Role in Deployment Pipeline

```
Chain definition (UI/import) → Runtime Catalog compiles → Camel XML (Handlebars) → Publishes to Consul KV → Engine detects update → Fetches full config → Creates Camel routes
```

### Verifying a change through the API

When testing, verifying, or reproducing a change through the HTTP API against the local
Docker stack — exercising import/export, chains, folders, deployment, or variables and
checking PostgreSQL and Consul side effects — apply the `runtime-catalog-api-testing`
skill.
